passages.title: Why Teenagers Need More Sleep
passages.body:
Many parents complain that their teenage children stay up late and are hard to wake in the morning. It is easy to think this is just laziness, but scientists say there is a biological reason. During the teenage years, the body starts producing melatonin, the hormone that makes us feel sleepy, about two hours later than it does in children or adults. As a result, most teenagers do not feel tired until eleven o'clock or even later.

At the same time, teenagers need between eight and ten hours of sleep a night to stay healthy. Because school usually starts early, many of them get only six or seven hours. Over time, this lack of sleep can affect their memory, their mood and even their exam results.

Some schools in other countries have tried starting classes later in the morning. In several studies, students at these schools were less tired, had better attendance and got slightly higher grades. However, a later start is not always possible, so experts also recommend simple habits: keeping phones out of the bedroom, going to bed at the same time every night and avoiding caffeine in the evening.

passages.title: Plastic in the Ocean
passages.body:
Every year, millions of tonnes of plastic end up in the world's oceans. Some of it is thrown directly into the sea, but most of it comes from the land. Rivers carry bottles, bags and food packaging from cities to the coast, and strong winds blow rubbish from beaches into the water.

Plastic is a serious problem because it does not disappear. Instead, sunlight and waves slowly break it into smaller and smaller pieces called microplastics. Fish and sea birds often mistake these pieces for food. When animals eat plastic, they may feel full but get no energy, and many of them die. Microplastics have also been found in the salt and seafood that people eat, although scientists are still studying how this affects our health.

There are no quick solutions, but there is a lot that can be done. Several countries have banned thin plastic bags, and some cities now charge customers for them. Clean-up groups collect rubbish from beaches every weekend. Most importantly, experts say, we need to use less plastic in the first place, for example by carrying our own bottles and shopping bags.

passages.title: The Silk Road
passages.body:
The Silk Road was not one single road. It was a network of trade routes that connected China with Central Asia, Iran, the Middle East and Europe for more than a thousand years. It got its name from Chinese silk, a very valuable cloth that people in the West were happy to pay a lot of money for.

Traders did not usually travel the whole route. Instead, goods passed from one merchant to another, and from city to city. Caravans of camels carried silk, spices, paper and porcelain to the west, while gold, glass, horses and wool travelled east. Iranian cities such as Neyshabur, Rey and Tabriz became rich and important because they were on these routes.

However, the Silk Road was about much more than buying and selling. Along with goods, travellers carried languages, religions, music, recipes and scientific knowledge. The technology for making paper, for example, moved from China to the Islamic world and later to Europe. In this way, the Silk Road helped different cultures learn from each other long before the age of the internet.

passages.title: Working from Home
passages.body:
Ten years ago, working from home was unusual for most office workers. Today, millions of people do at least part of their job from their living room or kitchen table. Fast internet and video-calling apps have made this possible, and many companies discovered during the pandemic that their employees could work well without being in the office every day.

For many workers, the biggest advantage is time. Without a long journey to work, they can sleep a little longer, spend more time with their families or exercise before starting work. Some people also say they can concentrate better at home because there are fewer interruptions from colleagues.

But working from home is not perfect. Some people feel lonely and miss chatting with their co-workers. Others find it hard to stop working, because their office is always just a few steps away. Managers sometimes worry that new employees learn more slowly when they cannot watch experienced colleagues at work. For these reasons, many companies now prefer a 'hybrid' model, where employees work from home on some days and come to the office on others.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the text?
options: Teenagers' sleep problems have biological causes and possible solutions.
Phones are the only cause of sleep problems.
questions.explanation_fa: متن توضیح می‌دهد که دیر خوابیدن نوجوانان دلیل زیستی دارد و بعد راه‌حل‌هایی پیشنهاد می‌کند.

options: They use their phones in bed.
questions.explanation_fa: the body starts producing melatonin ... about two hours later. این دلیل زیستی است که متن ذکر کرده.

questions.explanation_fa: teenagers need between eight and ten hours of sleep. شش یا هفت ساعت مقداری است که معمولاً می‌خوابند، نه مقداری که لازم دارند.

Leave the phone outside the bedroom.
